research_rationale:
Executive Order 13694 (Blocking the Property of Certain Persons Engaging in Significant Malicious Cyber-Enabled Activities; 80 FR 18077) is held in the Federal Register print (FR Doc. 2015-07788) and was read in full. The 22-clause inventory (the opening declaration and sections 1 to 10 with their paragraphs) matches the printed text. Four later orders amend the order: Executive Order 13757 of December 28, 2016, Executive Order 13984 of January 19, 2021, Executive Order 14144 of January 16, 2025 and Executive Order 14306 of June 6, 2025; the 2026 continuation notice names all four. Under the strike-and-insert ruling of 2026-10-21 each amendment is a later event on the clause it changes and the clause continues, amended, until the order ends. The order has no sunset or terminating condition of its own. A sentence-by-sentence search of the first 40 held texts that print the number 13694 (the lookup is capped at 40 files and reports itself truncated) found amendment language in the Executive Order 14306 print and its Federal Register copy, the Executive Order 13848 statement that this order remains in effect, and OFAC notices, and no revocation, supersession, rescission or repeal language aimed at this order. The Federal Register catalog search (later-events:ofr_catalog) returned amendment entries for Executive Orders 13757, 13984, 14144 and 14306 and cross-references between this order and the 2026 notice and Executive Orders 13848, 13849, 14110 and 14117; it returned no revocation or supersession of this order. The other general instrument in the packet, Executive Order 14294 of May 9, 2025 (Fighting Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations), does not print this number and states a prosecution policy for criminal regulatory offenses, which gives no reason to treat any clause as extinguished. Two other leads in the packet do not amend the order: the packet's machine leads from Executive Orders 14304 and 14315 do not print this number in their held texts, and Executive Orders 14110 and 14117 rely on the emergency this order declared but amend nothing in it (Executive Order 14110 was revoked in part by Executive Order 14148 according to the 2026 notice). The Executive Order 13848 print states that Executive Order 13694, as amended by Executive Order 13757, remains in effect. Because the order depends on a declared emergency, the 0 annual continuation notices held for it are attached to every clause; the last, the Notice of March 24, 2026, continues the emergency beyond April 1, 2026, which covers 2026-10-14. Every clause is operative on that date.
